title: Werewolves, Full Moons, and a New Game: Inside Robert Eggers' 'Werwulf'
summary:
What's scarier than a werewolf? A werewolf movie directed by the guy who made "The Witch" and "Nosferatu." Robert Eggers is back with "Werwulf," hitting theaters on Christmas Day.

The film is set in an English village in the 13th century. Aaron Taylor-Johnson plays a man who transforms into a werewolf every full moon. The cast also includes Willem Dafoe and Lily Rose-Depp — actors Eggers has worked with before.

Eggers says this is the darkest movie of his career. That's saying something, because his movies are already pretty creepy.

"After 'Nosferatu,' I kind of said, 'Let me try to write the scariest thing I can write,'" Eggers explained. "I don't know that I did that, but I definitely wrote the darkest thing."

He got the idea from historical werewolf stories he read starting in high school. In those old tales, people did such taboo things that their culture said, "You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf."

There's also a new trailer and an interactive game for fans to try. The official synopsis calls it "a harrowing tale of devotion, damnation, and the devil within." Creepy? Yes. Coming to theaters December 25.
why_it_matters: It shows how old stories and legends can still spark brand-new movies, and how the things that scare us are often the things that make us curious too.

background_read: Robert Eggers is an American filmmaker known for creepy, old-fashioned horror films such as 'The Witch' and 'Nosferatu,' which is why fans expect his werewolf movie to be extra scary.
Werewolf legends are very old — in old European stories, people believed that someone who broke their culture's rules could turn into a wolf.
A full moon is a real event in the sky that happens about once a month, which is why stories link it to werewolves.
